title: Which has more area, a square or equilateral triangles?
description: An equilateral triangle and a square share a side length. The triangle's height is less than its side, so the triangle, and also two triangles joined as a rhombus, have less area than the square.
teaching_notes: One idea: the height of a triangle is less than its slanting side, so its area is less than the square's. Watch for students who think equal sides mean equal areas.

video_script.why: The child uses area as base times the height drawn to the base, from the solved examples, to compare a square, a triangle and a rhombus with equal sides.
video_script.substitution: Compare each height with the side, because the height is shorter.
video_script.anchor: the book's equilateral triangle and square with the same side
video_script.payoff_line: The square is greater in both cases

final_answer.value: the square is greater in both cases
final_answer.spoken: the square is greater in both cases

hold_back: The square is greater in both cases
maths_rules: square of side s: area s × s
the height of an equilateral triangle of side s is a leg of a right triangle with longest side s, so it is less than s
triangle: 1/2 × s × h < 1/2 × s × s, less than half the square
two triangles form a rhombus with base s and height h < s: area s × h < s × s
check with s = 10: h = 5 × sqrt(3), about 8.66; triangle about 43.3, two about 86.6, square 100
video_script.design: A square, a triangle and a rhombus with the same side. Each height is shorter than the side.
open_questions: The worklist gives the reasons without a numeric check. The video adds a check with a side of ten, using the height of about eight point seven.

narration: <bookmark mark='ht'/>Step two, the height of the triangle is a leg of a right triangle.
<bookmark mark='long'/>That triangle has the side as its longest side, so the height is less than the side.
<bookmark mark='less'/>The area of the triangle is half of the side times its height. That is less than half of the side times the side.

narration: <bookmark mark='rh'/>Step three, two such triangles joined along a side make a rhombus.
<bookmark mark='pg'/>The rhombus is a parallelogram with the base equal to the side, and the same height as before.
<bookmark mark='less'/>Its area is the side times the height, which is less than the side times the side.
